changes.before: The store currently averages available session CER/WER values without weighting by reference length, and getSessions() retains completed sample sessions. For a corpus result, sum edit counts and reference lengths after explicitly excluding seeded data. Fixed dashboard cards are a separate presentation layer. [4, 10]
changes.after: The dedicated dashboard aggregator filters completed non-sample sessions before display. It computes corpus CER and WER from total edit counts divided by total reference units, counts exact raw and final line matches, and derives confidence, latency and error items from the same live records. The legacy global analytics method remains separate and is not used for the research dashboard. [4, 10]

changes.before: The primary recorded model result is validation CER 11.3388% at checkpoint step 16,900 on the declared 500-sample validation split. It is a model-handoff measurement and is distinct from the current dashboard overview cards. [1]
changes.after: The primary recorded model result remains validation CER 11.3388% at checkpoint step 16,900 on the declared 500-sample validation split. This model-handoff measurement remains separate from device-session analytics, whose values vary with the completed live records stored on the device. [1, 4, 10]

changes.before: The current research screen hard-codes its headline accuracy, AI comparison, dataset total and 500-line summary. Session history is loaded separately. Figures 4 and 10 therefore document the current interface; they are not used as experimental evidence. [10]
changes.after: The research screen no longer supplies headline accuracy, dataset totals, comparison gains, latency or confidence through fallback constants. When no verified live lines exist, metric cards show an em dash or an explanatory empty state. When verified lines exist, every displayed value is derived from the filtered session and line records. [4, 10]

changes.before: The 80% → 92% comparison is a 12-percentage-point change (15% relative). The separate 315/500 → 460/500 summary implies 63% → 92%, or 29 points. They cannot be combined as one experiment. Likewise, the displayed 2.3 seconds per image and 91.4% confidence require recorded runs and calibration before scientific interpretation. [10]
changes.after: The dashboard reports the change from raw exact-line accuracy to the selected final result in percentage points. Because the final selection can reflect both an AI suggestion and manual review, the interface labels this value as assisted workflow improvement rather than attributing the entire change to AI alone. [4, 10]
